correctness.rationale: Boundary-value ODEs yield three exact passage transforms; the renewal resolvent and retained-history inclusion–exclusion are exact. At a site detuned delta/sqrt(r/D), the three target transforms have exponentially small amplitudes exp(delta), exp(-delta) and their sum on the same r exp(-L sqrt(r/D)/2) time scale. Laplace continuity proves the full cover survival limit. Negative-argument renewal bounds control an exponential moment of both endpoint times, giving all positive moment convergence. Independent standard-library finite checks corroborate identities, though they cannot establish infinite-r claims.

value.rationale: Near the midpoint there are two competing equally distant rare targets, so the conventional single-farthest-target exponential completion approximation loses a degree of freedom. The Brownian displacement per reset sqrt(D/r) determines a physically natural (not arbitrary) detuning window. The resulting family gives non-exponential full cover-time laws, asymmetry-dependent moments, and a concrete geometric sensitivity law omitted by the known finite-rate mean-only theory; no broad paper-sized extension is required for this motivated sharp threshold crossover.
